chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawood al-Ajaly, a slave of Abu al-Maghra'a, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three have been given the power to hear the creatures: Paradise, the Fire, and the Maiden Houries. So when the servant prays and says: "O Allah, liberate me from the Fire, and admit me into Paradise, and marry me to the Maiden Houries," the Fire says: "O Lord, Your servant has asked You to emancipate him from me, so emancipate him." And Paradise says: "O Lord, Your servant has asked You for me, so settle him in me." And the Maiden Houries say: "O Lord, Your servant has proposed to You for us, so marry him to us." So if he finishes from his prayer and did not ask Allah for anything from this, the Maiden Houries say: "This servant is an ascetic regarding us." And Paradise says: "This servant is an ascetic regarding me." And the Fire says: "This servant is ignorant regarding me."'
ai.seo_question: What happens when a servant prays and asks for Paradise, Hellfire, and Houries?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *al-hayāt al-barzakhīyya* (life in the grave), attributing sensory faculties to Paradise, Hell, and the Houries to emphasize the efficacy of specific supplications (*du'a*) after prayer. It highlights the theological balance between asceticism (*zuhd*) and seeking divine bounty, warning that omitting these requests may indicate spiritual ignorance or a lack of desire for the ultimate rewards.
